title: Vessel level control and shutdown
goal: A reader can trace the vessel level regulation loop and the independent high-level inlet shutdown while distinguishing instrument locations, tags, and signal types.

rubric.must: The vessel V-101 outlet is visibly connected through LV-101 to the product tank, and LV-101 is identifiable as an actuated control valve.
The level measurement path connects V-101 to LT-101, then LIC-101, then the LV-101 actuator, with each endpoint identifiable.
LSHH-202 senses V-101 and has a separate signal path to the inlet shutoff valve XV-202 that does not pass through LIC-101 or LV-101.
Solid process piping, dashed electrical signals, pneumatic signals with diagonal marks, and dotted capillary sensing lines are visually distinguishable.
LT-101 and LSHH-202 have plain field instrument bubbles, while LIC-101 has a clearly visible control-room horizontal location mark.
LT-101, LIC-101, and LV-101 are readable as loop 101 tags, while LSHH-202 and XV-202 are readable as separate loop 202 tags beside or inside their own symbols.
FC is legible beside the XV-202 shutoff actuator and FO is legible beside the LV-101 outlet control actuator.

ideal.notes: Drafted by Codex from the source, the rubric and the pid exemplar, without seeing the engine's own output.

review.evidence: The drawing visibly presents both required functions: a traceable LT-101 → LIC-101 → LV-101 level-control loop and a separate LSHH-202 → XV-202 high-level shutdown path. Equipment, tags, locations, fail positions, and signal types are legible and consistent with the source.

items.evidence: Solid process piping visibly runs from the bottom of V-101 through actuated valve LV-101 and onward to TK-102.
A dotted capillary connects V-101 to LT-101, a dashed electrical line connects LT-101 to LIC-101, and a diagonally marked pneumatic line runs from LIC-101 to the LV-101 diaphragm actuator.
LSHH-202 is connected to V-101 by a dotted sensing line and has its own dashed electrical path to the XV-202 solenoid, separate from LIC-101 and LV-101.
The drawing and legend visibly distinguish heavy solid process piping, dashed electrical signals, diagonal-marked pneumatic signals, and dotted capillary or filled-system lines.
LT-101 and LSHH-202 appear as plain field bubbles, while LIC-101 has a visible horizontal control-room location mark and is positioned above the control-room/field boundary.
LT-101, LIC-101, and LV-101 are readable as loop 101; LSHH-202 and XV-202 are readable as the separate loop 202.
FC is legible beside the XV-202 actuator, and FO is legible beside the LV-101 actuator.
